1 Python files do not parse as Python 3, most likely Python 2. A rerun needs a Python 2.7 interpreter (end of life since 2020) or a port, and either is a logged deviation.

Python code imports linearmodels, matplotlib, nlopt, numba, numpy, pandas, scipy, seaborn, statsmodels but the package has no requirements file, environment file or lockfile. A rerun must choose versions and log them.
3 code lines use absolute paths from the authors' machines. A rerun must edit them, and each edit is a logged deviation.
61 scripts, no master script, and the README does not name an order. A rerun must choose one and log it.
Requires Matlab; the desk says it has it.

Files the code both writes and reads are already in the package: ../estimation/moments/means_health.pkl, ../estimation/moments/means_macro.pkl, ../estimation/moments/stds_health.pkl, ../estimation/moments/stds_macro.pkl, ../model/params/auxiliary.pkl, ../model/params/income_shocks.pkl, /model/params/sim_gdp_us.csv, output/eq_pus_ge3.pkl, output/moms.pkl, output/moms_sim.pkl. A run may read these instead of recomputing them. A receipt must say whether it replayed them or recomputed them, and a matching output hash alone does not show recomputation.
46 file reads use paths built at run time (macros, globs, variables), so triage could not check that those inputs exist.
No licence file and no licence named in the documentation. Running it for a check is unaffected, but a receipt should quote and hash files rather than redistribute them.
